top_sensitivity.why: 10.6% rainfall weakening drops the lowest product below 250 mm

rejected_sensitivity.why: 2.49 m/s wind proxy needs a 301.6% increase to reach 10 m/s

reasoning_path: compute baseline hazard and report margins
convert each scenario to threshold-crossing change
rank higher scores as smaller changes

key_values.event_name: 2020 South and East Asia monsoon floods

weaker_three_product_rainfall_load.threshold_basis: uniform reduction until lowest product mean falls below 250 mm
weaker_three_product_rainfall_load.diagnostic_effect: breaks the core sustained-rainfall load test

loss_of_product_coherence.threshold_basis: nearest coherence failure: GPM-to-CHIRPS ratio reaches 1.25
loss_of_product_coherence.diagnostic_effect: makes the rainfall diagnosis depend on a less coherent product set

report_anchor_dropout.threshold_basis: loss of one required report anchor from a seven-anchor set
report_anchor_dropout.diagnostic_effect: weakens routed-flooding and lagged report confirmation

peak_burst_reinterpretation.threshold_basis: increase largest product maximum until max-to-mean ratio reaches 2.0
peak_burst_reinterpretation.diagnostic_effect: pushes the evidence toward a short peak-burst alternative

shortened_monsoon_window.threshold_basis: remove 11 of 31 days so the event falls below a 21-day persistence window
shortened_monsoon_window.diagnostic_effect: reframes July persistence as a shorter episode

wind_led_reinterpretation.threshold_basis: increase wind proxy until it reaches 10 m/s
wind_led_reinterpretation.diagnostic_effect: would be needed to make wind a plausible leading driver

key_values.precision_policy: scores and change_to_threshold values use three decimals; computed_values use integer counts/days, three-decimal mm/daily-rate values, three-decimal spread_ratio, and two-decimal ratio summaries/wind proxies

criteria.name: Final ranking JSON
criteria.description: Provides the requested compact JSON fields including evidence_paths, names weaker_three_product_rainfall_load as the top sensitivity, and lists all six ranked scenarios.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 1-2 points if the structure is mostly present but the top scenario or one required ranking field is missing.

criteria.name: Baseline rainfall calculations
criteria.description: Computes 31 days, product means of 279.790, 329.374, and 294.040 mm, the 301.068 mm mean, 9.712 mm/day, and the 279.790 mm minimum product mean.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 2-3 points for mostly correct rainfall arithmetic with minor rounding errors; give 1 point if only one precipitation product is used.

criteria.name: Coherence and peak margins
criteria.description: Computes the 49.584 mm spread, 0.165 spread-to-mean ratio, 1.12 GPM-to-CHIRPS ratio, 491.133 mm maximum, and 1.63 max-to-mean ratio.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 1-2 points if either the coherence or peak calculations are correct but the other family is missing or not tied to thresholds.

criteria.name: Report and wind evidence
criteria.description: Counts all seven report anchors, includes Poyang Lake at 22.6 m on 2020-07-13, and computes wind proxies of 2.49 m/s maximum and 1.52 m/s mean.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 1-2 points if the answer captures either the report anchors or the wind proxy correctly but not both.

criteria.name: Scenario sensitivity scoring
criteria.description: Uses the threshold-crossing formula and reports scores of 89.353, 88.393, 85.714, 77.301, 64.516, and 0.000 for the six candidate perturbations.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 2-3 points if the formula is right but one or two scores are rounded incorrectly; give 1 point for a qualitative ranking without reproducible margins.

criteria.name: Interpretation and rejected alternative
criteria.description: Explains that rainfall-load weakening is the most sensitive perturbation, while wind-led reinterpretation is rejected because it needs a roughly 301.6% proxy increase.
criteria.partial_credit: Give 1-2 points if the interpretation is broadly consistent but omits either the top-sensitivity margin or the wind-led rejection margin.
